title: NRI Entrepreneur Dr Ronald Colaco Pitches 25-Year Coastal Master Plan for Karnataka
excerpt: Dr Ronald Colaco's proposal to the Karnataka government envisages an expert-led task force — including NRI representatives — and a 20–25-year master plan for the Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and Uttara Kannada coast.
body:
• NRI entrepreneur and philanthropist Dr Ronald Colaco has proposed a high-level Karnataka Coastal Tourism & Commercial Development Task Force to the state government.
  • The proposal, presented to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, calls for a 20–25-year integrated master plan for Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and Uttara Kannada.
  • The task force would include experts from planning, tourism, infrastructure, environment and finance — plus NRI representatives — and would study coastal development models from Dubai, Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Spain and Italy.
  • Environmental safeguards are central: protection of mangroves, wetlands and beaches, with zero untreated sewage discharge into the sea and backwaters.

A prominent NRI entrepreneur has put a 25-year vision for Karnataka's coastline on the state government's table. Dr Ronald Colaco, a leading philanthropist, has submitted a comprehensive proposal seeking the creation of a high-level Karnataka Coastal Tourism & Commercial Development Task Force for the integrated development of the state's coastal region, according to asiaPOST.

The Proposal

The proposal was presented to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar by Minister K.H. Muniyappa and MLC Dr Arathi Krishna in Bengaluru. Its goal: to position Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and Uttara Kannada as internationally competitive destinations for tourism, hospitality, trade, investment and employment.

Colaco wants the task force to be expert-led, comprising professionals from town planning, tourism, infrastructure, environment, ports, transport, finance and industry — along with NRI representatives. Its central job would be to prepare a 20–25-year Integrated Coastal Tourism and Commercial Development Master Plan, identifying areas suitable for sustainable development and creating a common framework for infrastructure and investment.

What It Would Build

The proposal envisages world-class waterfronts, marinas, promenades, tourism villages, resorts, convention centres, water transport networks, commercial hubs and logistics infrastructure at suitable coastal locations. Karnataka has more than 300 km of coastline, much of it underdeveloped relative to the tourism economies of Goa and Kerala — a gap the state government itself has acknowledged.

The timing fits a broader push. In September 2025, the Karnataka government announced it was working on a dedicated coastal tourism policy, with Tourism Minister H.K. Patil saying 40 strategic nodes had been identified for development and inviting private players to participate. A separate maritime masterplan envisages Rs 23,000 crore in investments across the coast, including a multipurpose port at Manki, an international cruise tourism port in Mangaluru, a water metro network in Mangaluru and coastal ferry services. The Kanara Chamber of Commerce and Industry has separately urged the state to put Mangaluru on the global tourism map with marinas, river tourism and Blue Flag beaches.

Green Strings Attached

A notable feature of Colaco's proposal is its emphasis on environmentally responsible development. It calls for the protection of mangroves, wetlands, forests, beaches and other ecologically sensitive areas, while insisting on zero untreated sewage discharge into the sea and backwaters. Modern sewage treatment plants, wastewater recycling, improved drainage systems and continuous water-quality monitoring are all part of the package.

Colaco has also suggested studying the coastal development models of Dubai, Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Spain and Italy — and adapting the relevant practices to Karnataka's environmental, legal and social conditions rather than copying them wholesale.

Why It Matters

Coastal Karnataka — often called the Silicon Beach of India — has been building an investment case for itself for years, from the TiECon Mangaluru startup conferences to a growing roster of angel investors and tech exits. But tourism infrastructure has lagged. A master plan with a 25-year horizon, backed by NRI capital and expertise, could change the region's trajectory — if the state government bites.

What to Watch

The proposal is just that for now: a proposal. Watch for the state government's response, whether the task force gets formally constituted, and how its mandate interacts with the coastal tourism policy and coastal tourism development board the government has already promised.
